title: Choose the visual world
question: Seasonal Emote Replacer: keep the dealt direction, take the alternate or the pick, or re-roll.

options.label: The Seasonal Window
options.lineage: Shop windows redressed every season by a window dresser and a sign painter
options.thesis: Your emote set is a shop window: dressed for the season, undressed after, same shop all year.
options.viewport: Enamel fascia with the name in gold leaf; below it the window glass holding your real set on shelves, with the sill as the working counter: channel input, season switch, 'Dress my window'.
options.risk: Turns into nostalgic costume if the lettering is timid or the glass becomes a flat picture; app screens must use the material, not shop props.

raised.raise: The window packs the real set edge to edge, dozens of emotes, never a sparse showcase of six.
Every emote sits in an identical shelf slot, so you read a set by sweeping the row.
Mapped, unmapped and conflict are marked by tag shape and stroke, never by colour alone.
Depth only from overlapping flat panes: no gradients, no glow.
The swap travels along the shelves in order, one slot at a time, exactly as the run does.

options.label: Alt-Art Binder
options.lineage: Trading-card binders and holiday alt-art holo variants
options.thesis: Every emote is a card and its seasonal version is the alt-art holo; the tool fills your binder.
options.viewport: An open binder spread: normal cards in the left page's pockets, their holo alt-arts on the right, channel input on the binder's index tab.
options.risk: Familiar: collectible-card nostalgia is where many runs land, and holo shimmer slides easily into gradient chrome.

options.label: Stream Desk Deck
options.lineage: Creator macro pads and desk instruments
options.thesis: Your set as a deck of keycaps; one orange key makes it seasonal.
options.viewport: A gunmetal deck fills the view: emotes on a keycap grid, a knurled season knob, an amber screen reading 'HALLOWEEN · 37/48 MAPPED', and the orange key.
options.case: Fuses tightly (set = key grid, season = knob, run = amber readout); streamers already own this object, so it wins on audience and ties on clarity.
options.risk: Can read as a hardware product page, and the keycap grid caps how big emote art can get.

options.label: Toy Catalogue Spread
options.lineage: Eighties toy catalogues in unmixed primaries
options.thesis: The set as a packed catalogue spread with burst flashes.
options.viewport: Emotes packed edge to edge on flat sweeps, a burst on every seasonal one.
options.case: Clear grid, but streamers don't recognise themselves in a toy catalogue.
options.risk: Reads as a retro shop pastiche.
options.kept: The courage to pack the field edge to edge.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: Sighting counts as a row of needles leaning into the red.
options.viewport: A row of meters, one per candidate.
options.case: Streamers know mixers, but meters don't say 'swap your emotes'.
options.kept: Identical units repeated as the ruler.

options.label: Darkroom Exposure Record
options.thesis: Sets as stacked translucent sheets with hatched regions.
options.viewport: Overlapping sheets over a zone ramp.
options.case: Alien to the audience and abstract for the task.
options.kept: State encoded without relying on hue.

options.label: Layered Papercut
options.thesis: Seasonal layers pasted over the normal set, peeled off to undo.
options.viewport: A symmetrical roundel of emotes built up in layers.
options.case: A lovely undo metaphor, but nothing in it reads as Twitch.
options.kept: Depth by overlap only, never by shading.

options.label: Versailles Vistas
options.thesis: A walk of axial reveals and fountains waking in sequence.
options.viewport: A garden plan seen from the terrace.
options.case: Wrong world for streamers, and no clarity gain.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark streamer-tool utility page done with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Centred headline and channel input over a screenshot of the tool, three feature cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other streamer tool, and close to Twitch's own look.
